### **Job Description and Duties**


Looking for innovative and impactful work in a fast\-evolving industry?  

  

The Department of Cannabis Control is seeking a motivated, detail\-oriented Environmental Scientist to join the Compliance Inspection Branch in the SoCal Office, LA South Unit. This position is primarily based in Los Angeles County and plays a critical role in ensuring environmental and operational compliance across California’s licensed cannabis facilities.  

  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (SES) (Supervisory) in the LA South Unit (Unit), within the SoCal Office (Office), part of the Compliance Inspection Branch (Branch), part of the Compliance Division (Division), within the Department of Cannabis Control (Department), the Environmental Scientist (ES) will perform scientific fieldwork and compliance evaluations across all licensed cannabis facilities. The incumbent will be responsible for verifying that licensed facilities are operating in accordance with applicable statutes, regulations, and environmental protection requirements. The incumbent will conduct on site inspections, technical assessments, and may participate in investigations within an assigned geographic area. The incumbent may also be required to perform coordinated fieldwork and investigations with other governmental agencies, as needed. The geographical location for this position is located within Southern California; however, may be required to conduct business throughout the State of California (State).  

  

Do you thrive in a fast\-paced environment?  

  

Join us and help advance California’s cannabis regulatory framework by supporting Division\-wide environmental, operational, and compliance oversight.  

  

What You’ll Do:  

  

Scientific Fieldwork \& Compliance Inspections
• Conduct onsite inspections of licensed cannabis facilities in Los Angeles County.
• Assess compliance with cannabis and environmental regulations and identify deficiencies.
• Prepare clear inspection reports with supporting documentation.
• Support coordinated inspections and search warrants with investigative or law enforcement entities.
• Communicate compliance findings to licensees, stakeholders, and internal staff.  

  

Records Review \& Scientific Evaluation
• Review operational records, inventory data, and tracking system information for compliance.
• Evaluate documentation related to water use, waste management, pesticides, storage, and transport.
• Apply scientific methods to identify non compliance and recommend corrective actions.
• Coordinate with regulatory and investigative partners on cases involving environmental or operational concerns.  

  

Communication, Coordination \& Education
• Collaborate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies on compliance matters.
• Provide guidance to licensees and industry representatives on environmental and operational requirements.
• Support educational and outreach efforts, including workshops and seminars.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Office of Legislative Affairs (OLA) is seeking a candidate who can blend scientific expertise with legislative insight to support policies that protect California communities from hazardous materials. This position offers a unique opportunity to work closely with the Legislature, translate complex technical information into clear guidance, and help shape high\-impact environmental policy. If you excel at science communication, legislative analysis, and strategic coordination, this role provides a meaningful way to advance OLA’s mission while influencing decisions that safeguard public health. Join us today!  

**As an Environmental Scientist you will have the opportunity to:**
* Receive, log, track, and respond to inquiries from legislative offices, advocacy groups, and regulated entities regarding legislation and DTSC’s programs and actions
* Coordinate with subject matter experts and program and executive staff to develop accurate, timely, and consistent responses
* Oversee the maintenance of a database of constituent inquiries and responses to promote accountability and identify recurring themes
* Review and analyze legislation that that could affect DTSC using an in\-depth scientific understanding of California’s manufacturers, businesses, hazardous materials, hazardous waste handling processes and procedures, and site mitigation practices to ensure the best legislative outcomes for DTSC and its mission
* Participate in meetings with legislative staff, stakeholders, and program experts to support communication of technical assistance
* Evaluate legislation from a technical perspective and work closely with DTSC program staff to ensure the legislation, if passed, can be adequately implemented as envisioned by the Legislature

**Desirable Qualifications We Look For:**
* Ability to clearly communicate complex scientific, technical, and regulatory information in writing and verbally to legislative offices, advocacy groups, and regulated entities
* Experience analyzing legislation related to hazardous materials, hazardous waste management, site mitigation, or chemical regulation, with skill in evaluating programmatic and fiscal impacts
* Demonstrated success coordinating work across multidisciplinary teams, ensuring timely, consistent, and accurate responses and briefing materials for legislative hearings and high\-profile departmental decisions
* Strong research, analytical, and strategic thinking skills, including the ability to identify emerging issues affecting/impacting environmental issues in California and analyze data using tools/databases (CalEnviroScreen, EnviroStor, GovBuddy, and Capitol Track) important for legislative analysis and engagement, and constituency affairs
* Excellent project management and organizational skills, with experience developing talking points, testimony packets, background materials, and follow\-up documentation for legislative engagements

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as a Third\-Party Risk Remediation Specialist, Core\+ and help strengthen service provider management, operational resilience and regulatory compliance across AIG Pacific.

**Make your mark in** **Enterprise Risk Management**


As well as helping customers to manage risks, AIG faces a wide array of our own risks every day. The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team partners across the AIG organization to inform strategic decision\-making and to facilitate rational risk\-taking that drives profitable growth. ERM ensures we have the right tools, processes and systems in place to identify, measure and manage our risks. As an ERM colleague, you can enhance your acumen by helping to shape and support our approach to risk.

**How you will create an impact**


You will support AIG Pacific’s Service Provider Management Remediation Program by coordinating and driving remediation activities across third\-party service provider and outsourcing arrangements. Working with Contract Owners, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, APAC / Global TPRM and business stakeholders, you will help improve ownership, data quality, monitoring and evidence of compliance with AIG framework requirements, APRA CPS 230 and relevant RBNZ expectations.


This is a 12\-month fixed\-term contract with the potential for extension, subject to business requirements.

**Key accountabilities include:**

* Support delivery of the 12\-month Service Provider Management Remediation Program across material service provider and outsourcing arrangements.
* Coordinate remediation activities including the service provider management platform (CBRA) uplift, service provider population review, materiality assessments, tiering, policy alignment, RACI embedment and reporting uplift.
* Work with Contract Owners and Business Owners to validate records, close data gaps and maintain an accurate Material Service Provider Register.
* Coordinate and facilitate CBRA activities and risk assessments undertaken by business stakeholders, including refreshes, material change triggers, contract renewals and service or data location changes.
* Support contract, monitoring and evidence uplift against AIG policy and regulatory expectations, working with Legal, Risk and business stakeholders.
* Prepare governance inputs, action tracking, issue escalation, remediation reporting and key risk themes for management, committees and Board reporting.
* Build and maintain effective working relationships across multiple stakeholders to drive timely completion of remediation activities and escalation of overdue actions.

**What you’ll need to succeed**

* Experience in third\-party risk, service provider management, operational risk, compliance, audit, vendor governance, procurement risk or regulatory remediation.
* Working knowledge of APRA CPS 230, CPS 220, CPS 234, FAR, outsourcing obligations or equivalent prudential risk practices is highly desirable.
* Strong remediation delivery skills, including action tracking, evidence management, risk assessments, control reviews and governance reporting.
* Exceptional organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines, stakeholders and competing priorities simultaneously.
* Ability to work confidently with business owners, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, Operations and regional or global risk teams to resolve issues and deliver outcomes.
* Clear written communication and analytical skills, with the ability to translate remediation progress into concise management reporting.


Applicants must have valid rights to work in Australia, as employer sponsorship is not available for this position.

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (SES) (Supervisory) in the LA South Unit (Unit), within the SoCal Office (Office), part of the Compliance Inspection Branch (Branch), part of the Compliance Division (Division), within the Department of Cannabis Control (Department), the Environmental Scientist (ES) will perform scientific fieldwork and compliance evaluations across all licensed cannabis facilities. • Support educational and outreach efforts, including workshops and seminars.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as a Third\-Party Risk Remediation Specialist, Core\+ and help strengthen service provider management, operational resilience and regulatory compliance across AIG Pacific.

**Make your mark in** **Enterprise Risk Management**


As well as helping customers to manage risks, AIG faces a wide array of our own risks every day. The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team partners across the AIG organization to inform strategic decision\-making and to facilitate rational risk\-taking that drives profitable growth. ERM ensures we have the right tools, processes and systems in place to identify, measure and manage our risks. As an ERM colleague, you can enhance your acumen by helping to shape and support our approach to risk.

**How you will create an impact**


You will support AIG Pacific’s Service Provider Management Remediation Program by coordinating and driving remediation activities across third\-party service provider and outsourcing arrangements. Working with Contract Owners, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, APAC / Global TPRM and business stakeholders, you will help improve ownership, data quality, monitoring and evidence of compliance with AIG framework requirements, APRA CPS 230 and relevant RBNZ expectations.


This is a 12\-month fixed\-term contract with the potential for extension, subject to business requirements.

**Key accountabilities include:**

* Support delivery of the 12\-month Service Provider Management Remediation Program across material service provider and outsourcing arrangements.
* Coordinate remediation activities including the service provider management platform (CBRA) uplift, service provider population review, materiality assessments, tiering, policy alignment, RACI embedment and reporting uplift.
* Work with Contract Owners and Business Owners to validate records, close data gaps and maintain an accurate Material Service Provider Register.
* Coordinate and facilitate CBRA activities and risk assessments undertaken by business stakeholders, including refreshes, material change triggers, contract renewals and service or data location changes.
* Support contract, monitoring and evidence uplift against AIG policy and regulatory expectations, working with Legal, Risk and business stakeholders.
* Prepare governance inputs, action tracking, issue escalation, remediation reporting and key risk themes for management, committees and Board reporting.
* Build and maintain effective working relationships across multiple stakeholders to drive timely completion of remediation activities and escalation of overdue actions.

**What you’ll need to succeed**

* Experience in third\-party risk, service provider management, operational risk, compliance, audit, vendor governance, procurement risk or regulatory remediation.
* Working knowledge of APRA CPS 230, CPS 220, CPS 234, FAR, outsourcing obligations or equivalent prudential risk practices is highly desirable.
* Strong remediation delivery skills, including action tracking, evidence management, risk assessments, control reviews and governance reporting.
* Exceptional organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines, stakeholders and competing priorities simultaneously.
* Ability to work confidently with business owners, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, Operations and regional or global risk teams to resolve issues and deliver outcomes.
* Clear written communication and analytical skills, with the ability to translate remediation progress into concise management reporting.
